source_ref: C++ Core Guidelines, draft standard and Godot C++ documentation

entries.content: Tie resource lifetime to object lifetime so cleanup follows normal scope and exception paths. Prefer RAII wrappers over manual acquire/release pairs for owned resources.
Use std::unique_ptr when one owner controls a dynamically allocated object. It documents ownership in the type system and avoids manual delete paths.
Use shared_ptr only when lifetime is genuinely shared between independent owners. Do not introduce reference-counted ownership merely to avoid deciding who owns an object.
If member types already manage their own resources correctly, avoid writing custom destructor/copy/move operations. The rule of zero reduces lifetime bugs and keeps semantics composable.
Initialize objects before use and prefer declarations close to the value that initializes them. Uninitialized state should not be used as an implicit control-flow mechanism.
Declare data const or constexpr when mutation is not intended. This documents invariants and reduces the writable state an implementation must reason about.
std::vector stores elements contiguously and provides amortized constant-time insertion at the end. Middle insertion/erasure is linear, so choose algorithms with those costs in mind.

If an upper or expected element count is known before a hot operation, reserve enough vector capacity to reduce reallocations. Do not call reserve repeatedly with tiny increases inside the same growth loop.

In per-frame, physics and audio paths, avoid avoidable heap allocation, blocking I/O and verbose logging. Preallocate/reuse buffers and move diagnostics outside the timing-sensitive loop when possible.
Prefer narrow interfaces that expose the operation a caller needs rather than broad access to internal mutable state. This reduces coupling and makes ownership and invariants easier to maintain.

entries.topic: Use scoped enums for state domains
entries.content: Use enum class for closed state/value domains when practical so enumerators remain scoped and accidental integer conversion is avoided.

entries.topic: Use the project godot-cpp build contract
entries.content: Build and load the native extension using the project-supported godot-cpp/SCons contract. Do not substitute an ad-hoc compiler invocation without matching the required include paths, ABI options and .gdextension binary mapping.

Native classes intended for Godot must be registered through the extension initialization path and expose intended methods/properties through Godot bindings. Keep registration explicit so missing classes fail early at load/scene validation.

Do not trade maintainability for speculative micro-optimization. Identify the hot path with profiling or timing evidence, optimize the measured bottleneck, then compare behavior/performance against a baseline.
